excerpt: Institute of International Studies (IIS‐RU), Ramkhamhaeng University RU Printing Press, Ramkhamhaeng Road, Huamark, Bangkapi, Bangkok 10240 International phone +66 2310 8895, e‐mail info@iis.ru.ac.th JR 301 – Computer‐assisted Reporting (CAR) Prerequisite: none Course Syllabus Lecturer: Professor Ulrich Werner E‐mail: ulrich.werner@iis.ru.ac.th Schedule and room: August 4 and 27, 2008: Tha Chai building, room 504 August 6, 11, 13, 18, 20, and 25, VKB building, computer center Office Hours: All course days and by appointment Course Description: 3 Credits This course introduces practically to the data research and data analysis skills that students and professional journalists need to write better stories. The course focuses on research on the Internet in search engines, specialised search engines, e‐book libraries, and online databases. Students gain hands‐on experience in applied research supported by a well‐founded theoretical background. Course Structure Each class day focuses on a different subject. It begins with introduction and exhibition of the particular subject, followed by a project in which students individually apply the subject matters on a given topic. Textbook In this course, we use online sources. Additional text will be handed out during the course. Course Web Site The course Web site is http://sites.goole.com/a/iis.ru.ac.th/jr301‐2008/ If you have an IIS e‐mail account, you can log in to http://intranet.iis.ru.ac.th and reach the site from there. Instructional Methods The material in this course will be conveyed through lectures, various reading assignments, class discussions, and case analysis, but there is a clear focus on structured skill‐building exercises. Class Attendance This project‐oriented course makes full class attendance crucial. It will be difficult to catch up for a day if you missed the introduction in the morning. On the course Web site, an overview will be provided for each day, enhanced by links to resources and handed‐out material, if any. Class Hours Classes begin at 9.00 hrs and end at 16.00 hrs. Classes may end earlier in order to give students time to do their assignments. Those students coming later than 9.00 hrs will miss the subject basics and introduction of that day. They cannot expect to receive special support from the lecturer since first those students will receive support who arrived in time. Plagiarism Since the final project will be a written paper resulting from own research on a given topic, plagiarism is an important topic in this course. The policies of Ramkhamhaeng University and the Institute of International Studies do not accept any plagiarism or copyright violation. Please be aware of the plagiarism policy in the IIS Student Handbook, which is available for download on the IIS Web site (http://www.iis.ru.ac.th). It is crucial to correctly reference all sources. Any attempt of cheating, or any violation of the plagiarism policy, will definitely result in failing this course. Final Project The final project is a written assignment about a research topic. This topic will be announced on the morning of August 25, 2008 (the day before the last course day). Each student will discuss the topic individually and do the necessary research on his/her own.
